versions.one_liner: Fires negatively on punctuation immediately after a closing bold/italic marker (** or *) in chat or list contexts.
versions.trigger_hypothesis: Strong negative activation on punctuation (comma, period) that immediately follows a closing bold/italic marker (** or *) within chat or list contexts, especially in numbered/bulleted items or after emphasized phrases.
versions.output_hypothesis: The neuron may mark the end of a stylistically emphasized segment, suppressing continuation after bold/italic text in formatted content.
alternatives: negative on punctuation after any alphanumeric token in a list
negative on punctuation after quoted text
versions.adapter_changes: State n_amp+1 shows dramatically stronger negative activations in chat/emotional contexts; o_sup+1 often reduces negative magnitude.

versions.author: deepseek/deepseek-v3.2
versions.label: strong negative on punctuation and certain words
versions.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron fires strongly negative on punctuation tokens (comma, period) and certain words like 'where' and '1' when they appear in specific syntactic positions, often at the end of a phrase or before a continuation.
versions.output_hypothesis: The neuron suppresses continuation of a phrase or list, possibly to signal a boundary or to reduce the probability of certain tokens.
alternatives: The neuron detects the end of a clause or sentence.
The neuron responds to specific tokens regardless of context.
versions.adapter_changes: State C+1 shows dramatically increased negative activation in chat/emotional_chat segments (W19-W23), suggesting the adapter amplifies the boundary-detection signal in assistant responses. Other states have minimal changes.
